ABOUT THE ROLE: As a Network Operations Center (NOC) Specialist, you are the eyes and the voice of the campus — never the hands. You watch campus health signals around the clock, detect and verify site-impacting events, assemble the right responders fast, and run incident communications leadership can trust. You make sure no major incident closes without a timeline, a report, and a tracked corrective project. This is a communications-and-judgment role at the center of site operations, not a junior-engineering holding pen. You do not do wrench work, plant operation, deep root-cause analysis, monitoring design, technical SEV command, or tool building — those belong to SiteOps, Facilities, Hardware Failure Analysis, Site SRE, and Software Platforms. Detect, verify, and escalate within time budgets; operate the escalation matrix (NOC → on-call SRE → domain owners) and page correctly the first time. Proven ability to acknowledge, classify, and escalate incidents under SLA in a high-signal environment. Experience opening and running incident bridges, including stakeholder updates on a fixed cadence and live timeline hygiene. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to write clear updates while an incident is in progress. Demonstrated pattern recognition across multiple domains (compute, network, storage, and/or facilities signals) and curiosity about how those systems interact. Experience following, maintaining, and improving operational process (runbooks, escalation matrices, handoffs, or similar). Willingness and ability to work a rotating shift schedule, including nights and weekends, as part of continuous campus coverage. PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: Prior NOC, data center operations, or campus reliability experience in a high-performance computing, AI/ML infrastructure, or large-scale production environment. Experience writing major-incident reports and driving corrective follow-ups to closed (e.g. tickets, projects, or Linear). Familiarity with Linear or similar work-tracking tools for corrective action programs. Experience partnering with SRE, SiteOps, and Facilities on escalations and post-incident follow-through. Participation in game days, tabletop exercises, or runbook improvement programs. Prior work in a fast-paced startup or tech company like SpaceXAI. SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. Examples Of Job Duties PBX Technician Provide customer service, troubleshooting, educate customers on available ACS products and services, provision and de-provision products and services. Answer customer inquiries. Determine cable distribution to fulfill service requirements. Run, secure and terminate necessary cabling. Place equipment cabinets, racks, or supporting frame work. Accomplish all inter-cabinet wiring. Install associated sets and sub-sets of business systems. Install associated power equipment and make necessary distribution. Install and provision system programming. Perform all facets of fault location of PBX, PAX, Key, VoIP telephone or special circuits to restore degraded or out-of-service conditions. Conduct system or sub-system testing as required to determine failures or to accomplish routine maintenance tests. Perform preventative maintenance and database backups Install, maintain, and modify PBX and Key Systems. Installation and configuration of vendor specific cards and equipment Central Office Technician Identify, research and resolve software and switch issues daily Use applicable interface devices and appropriate test equipment to monitor digital central offices and associated facilities. Make decisions and take actions to insure uninterrupted service. Respond to system messages and associated alarms to determine the root cause of network problems and to take appropriate corrective action. Analyze switch performance, system faults, customer reports, initiating corrective actions when necessary. Perform routine testing both on site and from remote test facilities, sometimes coordinating with other departments, customers, and other interconnecting telco personnel. Maintain technical documentation, office records, drawings, archived printouts, and site logs. Interpret and input complex software translation changes for system upgrades. Perform preventative maintenance and database backups. Installation, configuration and provisioning of all Remote and Central Office equipment. Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain Central Office equipment and wiring. Perform other duties as assigned. Data Technician Perform all associated installation, maintenance and testing on private line and special circuit equipment, digital access cross connect systems, T-carrier, fiber optic terminal and multiplexer equipment. Install, align, and maintain line treatment equipment associated with data and analog circuits. Installation and maintenance of central office and customer premise equipment to include but not limited to: WAN/LAN Ethernet switches, routers, servers and VTC equipment. Perform all line conditioning testing; along with end-to0end tests for installation of data transport equipment from the Central Office to customer premise, utilizing a variety of basic and complex test equipment, and switch and system based testing facilities to ensure proper installation and testing of new systems. Coordinate installation activities with all customers and departments to include manufacturers if required to a successful completion. Make cross-connect changes and re-arrangement on MDF’s, digital cross connect panels, and fiber distribution frames as required. Interpretation of engineering specifications, schematics, and drawings associated with AK Communications network and CPE installations. Perform other duties as assigned. Customer and Network Support Technician (CNST) Responsible for monitoring the network, and are critical to resolving customer service trouble issues and verifying with customers that their issues are resolved. Receive phone calls and accept trouble tickets/reports from our Tier I trouble resolution team, managed and strategic customers, Wireless roaming partners, Tier III workgroups and other sources. Responsible for the customer’s trouble and manages communication with the customer from the time the report/ticket is received until the issue is resolved. Use a variety of systems and tools to isolate the customer’s trouble and either resolve or escalate the issue to the appropriate Tier III resource for resolution. In addition to Tier II customer support responsibilities, the CNST will operate the Alaskan Network Operation Center. Receive and resolve all Tier II support escalations for ACS products and services. Examples of products and services include but are not limited to ACS offerings in Wireline, Wireless, Enterprise, Internet and Long Distance suites. Network Management Systems Support – NOC Admin Engineer, operation, administration and support of OSS/BSS equipment and databases. Configuration Management of operating systems of network equipment and support servers used within the Network Operations Center. Installation, Troubleshooting and Problem solving of systems, desktops, and equipment used in delivering services by the NOC. Perform other duties as assigned. Minimum Qualifications Minimum Education and Experience Required You must have a high school diploma and must possess and maintain a driver’s license. Network Technicians are normally required to have and maintain vendor specific training and/or certifications. Network Technicians are required to have four (4) years training in a relevant telephone apprentice program or equivalent experience leading to journeyman level performance in this specialty, with two (2) years experience in the skills and work this position will typically perform. This position may travel by Air, Land and Sea by commercial and non-commercial means to deliver service to Alaska Communications Customers located in remote areas of Alaska. Certifications And Licenses Required External applicants must successfully pass a pre-employment suitability assessment and either a DOT or non-DOT drug test, depending on position. Network Technicians outside of Anchorage, may be required to perform duties of a Field Technician, which may require a Medical Certification or a CDL. Additional Job Requirements External applicants must successfully pass a pre-employment suitability assessment and drug test. We hope you’ll join us as we change lives through technology.

The project also provides strategic and technical assistance to strengthen malaria programming and systems and national and subnational capacities for preparedness and response to public health emergencies and infectious disease threats. Across these areas, RISE emphasizes strengthened government leadership, effective use of data, resilient health systems, and sustainable transition to country ownership. The Technical Director provides strategic and technical leadership for the implementation of life-saving interventions under the RISE project in Angola. S/he will provide technical and programmatic oversight and direction across HIV, malaria, and emergency preparedness/Global Health Security, with a focus on community health programs, health systems strengthening, integrated disease response, and transition towards sustainable government-led programming. S/he is responsible for ensuring that the program follows evidence-based approaches and is aligned with national priorities and donor expectations. This position reports to the RISE Project Director/Country Program Manager and plays a critical role in guiding the project’s overall technical direction, fostering strong stakeholder relationships, liaising with the Ministry of Health (MoH) and other relevant health departments and agencies, and ensuring integration and synergy across technical areas and with national counterparts. The Technical Director will also work closely with the Project Director to support overall project management, including liaising with donors, MOH and other stakeholders in the Project Director’s absence; tracking project progress against workplan activities; and ensuring implementation aligns with the approved scope, timeline and budget. The Technical Director will play a critical role as a member of the RISE Project Senior Management Team and contribute to strategic and programmatic decision-making. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership & Project Management Provide high-level technical and programmatic leadership and support the Project Director/Country Program Manager in setting the strategic direction for the project across HIV, malaria, emergency preparedness/Global Health Security, and cross-cutting health systems strengthening. Ensure project alignment with MOH and U.S. Department of State priorities, incorporating stakeholder feedback into program design and implementation and ensuring project activities are consistent with USG guidance. Support project planning, implementation, and reporting, ensuring timelines, objectives, and deliverables are met. Support development of annual work plans, budgets, and routine implementation plans across the project’s technical areas. Ensure delivery of required reports and deliverables that meet donor requirements and project objectives. Collaborate closely with finance and project staff to track project budgets and ensure delivery within approved budget, scope, and timelines. Support the Project Director/Country Program Manager in tracking project performance against targets and workplan activities and use adaptive management approaches to adjust project activities as required to meet targets and deliverables. In collaboration with the Senior MEL Advisor, provide technical leadership to the project team in the areas of data use for decision-making and the use of epidemiological and programmatic data to prioritize interventions and activities across HIV, malaria, and public health emergency preparedness and response. Promote integration and coordination across disease-specific and health systems activities to maximize efficiency, sustainability, and government ownership. Technical Expertise & Quality Assurance Lead the design and delivery of high-quality interventions covering HIV, malaria, emergency preparedness/Global Health Security, infectious disease response, and health systems strengthening, with an emphasis on sustainability and transition to government leadership. Provide overall technical oversight across the project’s portfolio, working closely with technical leads and subject-matter experts to ensure strong technical quality within each program area. Ensure project activities are evidence-based, data-driven, and aligned with relevant international and national standards, policies, strategies, and guidelines. Promote linkages between emergency preparedness/GHS activities and broader health system strengthening, including surveillance, laboratory systems, data systems, supply chain, workforce capacity, and coordination mechanisms, as applicable to the project scope. Oversee and mentor technical and project staff to identify and integrate innovative approaches to strengthen disease prevention, preparedness, detection, and response. Provide technical and programmatic oversight and strategic direction and ensure appropriate technical support for implementation of program activities. Provide overall leadership for data-based decision-making, using adaptive management approaches for prioritization of resources and targeted implementation. Stakeholder & Partnership Engagement Ensure project activities are coordinated with national, provincial, municipal, and community-level health initiatives, contributing to an integrated and government-led response. Work closely with MOH, including relevant HIV, malaria, epidemiological surveillance/emergency preparedness programs and structures, as well as CSOs, NGOs, FBOs, and other stakeholders to improve coordination, communication, and collaboration. Alongside the Project Director/Country Program Manager, develop and oversee the project’s implementation plans at national, provincial, municipal, and community levels, supporting implementation tracking and ensuring activities are aligned with the workplan and budget. Track project performance indicators, document lessons learned, and adapt strategies as necessary to improve impact and sustainability. Alongside the Project Director/Country Program Manager and senior project team, prepare and submit high-quality reports to the donor detailing project achievements, challenges, and recommended actions. Provide technical oversight and direct support to sub-partners implementing under the project and ensure their activities are evidence-based, data-driven, and aligned with applicable international, national, donor, ethical, and technical standards, including requirements applicable to HIV, malaria, and GHS programming. Represent the program in relevant technical working groups and national, subnational, and community forums related to HIV, malaria, emergency preparedness/Global Health Security, and health systems strengthening, as appropriate. Build and maintain effective working relationships with senior government counterparts and technical partners to strengthen coordination, government leadership, and sustainability. Team Management & Capacity Building Train and supervise project technical staff, ensuring team members across the project’s technical portfolio have the skills, guidance, and support needed to perform effectively. Provide oversight for required technical mentoring and capacity-building opportunities for technical staff and provincial-based teams and foster a collaborative and supportive working environment. Promote collaboration and integration among technical leads responsible for HIV, malaria, emergency preparedness/GHS, MEL, supply chain, and other cross-cutting areas. Provide leadership and mentorship on data-driven decision-making, including regular data reviews that drive prioritization and implementation. Promote adherence to ethical standards and protocols, ensuring staff safety and community well-being throughout project activities. Be a steward and role model of Jhpiego’s internal Culture of Respect, ethics and safeguarding standards, and organizational values. Required Qualifications Required Qualifications Clinical background required (MD or nursing); MPH or other advanced degree in a health-related field preferred. A minimum of 10+ years of relevant experience, including at least 5 years of experience in senior technical leadership positions and managing or providing technical leadership to large-scale USG-funded projects (PEPFAR, DoS, CDC, or similar). Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills; demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with government agencies, donors, technical partners, and community groups. Proven experience in the technical leadership of HIV, malaria, Global Health Security/emergency preparedness, and/or other infectious disease programs, including strategic planning, technical oversight, quality assurance, and performance management. Direct technical expertise in all three areas is not required, but demonstrated ability to provide strategic oversight across multidisciplinary technical portfolios is essential. Experience working with national or subnational disease programs, surveillance and/or emergency preparedness structures, and health system strengthening initiatives strongly preferred. Strong experience in programmatic and operational management, including annual planning, target monitoring, budget oversight, and preparation of technical reports for donors. Proven ability to use programmatic and epidemiological data for strategic decision-making, geographic prioritization, and adaptive management. Experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) applied to continuous quality improvement and programmatic impact. Experience with digital health tools and platforms for data analysis and use is an asset. Strong strategic and technical leadership skills, including supervision of multidisciplinary teams and institutional capacity development. Experience providing technical guidance to teams and implementing partners, ensuring compliance with technical, ethical, and operational standards. Ability to manage multiple technical priorities in complex environments, demonstrating a high level of autonomy, accountability, and results-oriented focus. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and communicate complex data effectively. Excellent organizational and project management skills, with attention to detail. Ability to work in a multicultural environment and build collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders. Excellent verbal, written, interpersonal, and presentation skills in English and Portuguese. Experience working with senior MOH officials, NGOs, FBOs, CBOs, and other national and international health stakeholders.
